atoms.text: Now, Dusty wants to see how food gets from the farm onto our plate. Let’s see how cheese is made!

instruction.text: We’re back on the farm. Select the animal we get our milk from.

feedback.end: Most of our milk comes from cows. It’s used to make lots of different food - for example, cheese, butter, yoghurt and cream. These are called dairy products.

feedback.correct: Great! Cows have udders, which farmers squeeze to get milk from. This can be collected in a bucket.

atoms.a: “What can we use to collect milk from the cow?“
atoms.sound: ssml:<voice voiceLang='en' voice='m8'>What can we use to collect milk from the cow?</voice>

instruction.text: Answer Dusty’s question by listening to the options and selecting the correct answer.

atoms.a: “Now we need to bring the milk to the cheese factory. How do we get there?”
atoms.sound: ssml:<voice voiceLang='en' voice='m8'>Now we need to bring the milk to the cheese factory. How do we get there?</voice>

b.sound: Follow the road north, then turn left and then turn right.
Keep following the road north and don’t turn anywhere.

instruction.text: We made it to the factory. This machine turns milk into cheese. Select the milk to learn more.

feedback.end: Milk doesn’t just magically turn into cheese! Cultures and rennet need to be mixed in with the milk, and then the machines heat it up and stir it.

instruction.text: Next, the cheese is left to ripen. Select the image of ripened cheese.

feedback.finish: Food isn’t always immediately ready after some machine work. Cheese needs to be left to ripen for weeks or months before it’s ready!
feedback.wrong: This is milk that hasn’t been made into cheese.

instruction.text: Finally, the cheese is taken to a supermarket, and we can buy it. Drag the cheese slice into the basket.

text.text: After a long journey, your cheese is finally ready for eating! Farms and factories work together to make lots of the food you see in the supermarket.
